key_idea: Put a lifted tensor code on the squares of a left-right Cayley complex, so that the tensor code's agreement testability in each vertex link, combined with expansion of the parallel random walk on edges, makes local disagreements spread and get caught by a constant-query tester.
reason: The left-right Cayley complex is a striking, natural object, and the local-to-global argument is conceptual: agreement testability in the links plus expansion of the edges-to-edges walk explains why a constant-query test works. The cost is sizeable bookkeeping: constant chasing, a self-correction algorithm analysed in two propositions, separately built base codes, and degree reduction on LSV/Morgenstern generators, all of which keep it below book-proof level.
recognized: Dinur–Evra–Livne–Lubotzky–Mozes, 'Locally Testable Codes with Constant Rate, Distance, and Locality' (c^3-LTCs via left-right Cayley complexes)
